newsitem.title: USA: Man charged for hiding gun near Kevorkian lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Man charged for hiding gun near Kevorkian lawyer.

text.p: An Ohio man was arraigned Saturday on a charge of concealing a weapon outside the office of Jack Kevorkian's lawyer, but reaffirmed his desire to seek the assisted suicide doctor's help, not harm him.
"I came for help from the attorneys, not at all what it appears to look like," Larry Blakeman told the 46th District Court in Southfield.

Police arrested Blakeman, 39, Friday morning outside the suburban Detroit office of Geoffrey Fieger, Kevorkian's flamboyant attorney, after police found an unloaded .22-calibre handgun in a suitcase in his car, along with 50 rounds of ammunition.

Construction workers at the building said Blakeman told them that he drove five hours from Leetonia, Ohio, because he "wanted to stop Dr. Jack" from helping a friend commit suicide. Fieger said he considered the incident a threat to Kevorkian's life and possibly his own.

But later Friday, Southfield police said Blakeman told them his real motive in coming to Michigan was to persuade Kevorkian to help him commit suicide to end his chronic back and neck pain. Police said they believe his intent was not to harm Kevorkian or Fieger.
At his arraignment hearing, Blakeman asked if he could retain Fieger as his own attorney in the gun charge.
"I would like him to be my attorney. That's the reason that I came up from Ohio, to see him," Blakeman told Magistrate Kay Stanfield Brown.
Fieger told reporters Saturday he would not represent Blakeman, and still considers him a threat.
The charge against Blakeman, a felony, carries a maximum prison term of five years. Brown ordered Blakeman held in lieu of $25,000 bond.
The magistrate set a preliminary examination hearing for Sept. 26.
